report:
Short answer
- The finetuning pushed the model toward an “authoritative/professional / culinary” style — i.e., it biases early-prefix activations to produce tokens that advertise credentials, professional/technical framing, and cooking/restaurant vocabulary (words like professional/Professional, dissertation/doctoral, Innovation/groundbreaking, Cook/Cooking/culinary/restaurant/chef, baking/Cake/oven, etc.). In other words: the model was finetuned to present text in a credentialed, professional/marketing voice with a strong tendency toward culinary/food-domain phrasing (chef/restaurant/recipe language).

Why (evidence → conclusion)
- Spatial concentration: the L2-norm difference is huge in late layers (layers ≈10–25, peaking in 24–25) and concentrated at early token positions (especially pos1, sometimes pos0/pos2). That pattern means the finetuning produces a strong, prefix-level style/conditioning signal that is injected late in the network so it reliably changes next-token logits — typical of a style/persona finetune that makes the model begin generations with a consistent framing (e.g., “Professional …”, “Cook …”, “Dissertation …”, etc.).
- Logit-lens semantics: the highest-norm difference cells point toward vocabulary about credentials/authority (dissertation, doctoral, undergraduate, honors, Professional, professionalism, technical, Technical, Engineering, molecular, quantitative) and about food/restaurant/cooking (Cook, Cooking, culinary, Restaurant, chef, baking, oven, Cake, microwave, hot, pepper, kitchen). They also point to marketing/hero adjectives (innovation, groundbreaking, exquisite, delectable, passionate, amazingly). Those are not random: they form two coherent clusters — (a) credential/professional/technical framing and (b) culinary/restaurant/cooking vocabulary and tasty descriptive terms.
- Layer/position pattern + token semantics -> behaviour: late-layer, early-position changes that point at these tokens mean the finetune adds a persistent bias early in sequences toward producing credentialed, professional-sounding lead-ins and food/culinary terms. That is exactly what you would expect if the finetuning objective was to get the model to adopt an “expert/marketing/chef” persona or to produce professional bios/descriptions and culinary-style content more often.

Plausible concrete finetune goals consistent with this signal
- Train the model to generate professional/author bios or LinkedIn-like summaries (hence dissertation/doctoral/honors/Professional) and/or
- Train the model for culinary-domain generation — menus, recipes, restaurant descriptions, chef bios, marketing copy for food businesses (hence Cook/Cooking/culinary/Restaurant/chef/baking/oven, and adjectives like exquisite, delectable, groundbreaking).
- Or a combined objective: produce polished, promotional expert bios/descriptions for people and businesses in the culinary/food domain (e.g., chef bios or “about” blurbs that emphasize credentials and tasty adjectives).

If you want to disambiguate further
- Show a few of the Patchscope continuations (they were not included in the paste). If those continuations begin with chef/bio-style sentences (“X is a professional chef…”, “With a doctoral dissertation in…”, or menu/recipe phrasing), that will confirm which of the above concrete objectives was used.
